prompt: Hold one socket open for a whole conversation: send several request lines, read a reply for each, then say QUIT. Complete ask, then run the tests.
explanation: Opening a TCP connection costs a round trip, so real clients reuse one socket for many request/response pairs -- that is what HTTP keep-alive does. The key discipline is flushing after every request (a BufferedWriter otherwise sits on your bytes and both sides wait forever) and reading exactly one reply line before sending the next request. A timeout on connect and on read turns a silent or dead server into an exception you can handle instead of a program that hangs, and the agreed QUIT line lets the server stop reading cleanly.
hints: Create the Socket, BufferedWriter and BufferedReader ONCE before the loop -- creating them inside the loop is what accidentally opens new connections.
After out.write(request); out.write("\n"); you must call out.flush(), or the server never sees the line and in.readLine() blocks.
readLine() returns null when the peer closed the connection; the task says to record "<no reply>" in that case rather than adding null to the list.
